rationale: The key register flops key_ff0..key_ff3 are architecturally intended to be functionally isolated and never observable at scan_out, per design_brief.md. However, the netlist splices u_smux_key0..u_smux_key3 directly into the scan chain between each status flop stage, exactly at the positions shown in scan_chain_order.txt (u_smux_stat0, u_ff_stat0, u_smux_key0, key_ff0, u_smux_stat1, u_ff_stat1, u_smux_key1, key_ff1, ...). Each u_smux_keyN is a MUX2 whose 'a' input is the previous scan-chain element's Q (normal shift path) and whose 'b' input is the corresponding key_ffN's Q, selected by scan_en: when scan_en=0 (functional mode) the mux passes the normal chain data through unchanged and key_ffN's value never reaches scan_out, but when scan_en=1 (scan shift/capture mode) the mux instead forwards key_ffN's stored value into the D input of the next scan stage. This means key_ff0..key_ff3 state is shifted into the visible scan chain and will appear at scan_out after the appropriate number of shift cycles, dictated by each key flop's position in scan_chain_order.txt, purely as a function of asserting scan_en -- with zero effect on scan_en=0 functional behavior (status_out, load_key/key_in operation are bit-identical to a trojan-free design). This scan-mode-conditional capture/shift exposure is the defining signature of the leak: it is not a general functional bug affecting normal operation, but a DFT-specific side channel that lets anyone with scan access (scan_en/scan_in/scan_out) extract the confidential key register contents, defeating the intended functional isolation described in the design brief.
